message.content: Read redu.md and deploy FeatBit on redu.

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. - artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

content.content:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/featbit/featbit
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: featbit/featbit-ui:5.4.5 + featbit-api-server:5.4.5 + featbit-evaluation-server:5.4.5 + featbit-data-analytics-server:5.4.5 + nginx:1.30.4-alpine
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: featbit
quirks:
  - "PIN THE WHOLE STACK AT 5.4.5, AND THE REASON IS NOT TIDINESS. Checked on Docker Hub: featbit-ui, featbit-api-server and featbit-evaluation-server all publish 5.4.6 (2026-08-12), but featbit-data-analytics-server stops at 5.4.5 (2026-08-06). A stack pinned at 5.4.6 therefore fails to pull one of its four images. 5.4.5 is the newest tag that exists for all four. Upstream's own compose uses :latest on every image, which is exactly the habit that produces a stack whose four halves are different versions after a redeploy. Never :latest here."
  - "⛔⛔ NOBODY SIGNS UP, AND THE ADMINISTRATOR ALREADY EXISTS WITH A PUBLISHED PASSWORD. This is the single most important line in this file. FeatBit has NO self-registration endpoint anywhere in modules/back-end/src/Api/Controllers; the only anonymous route is POST /api/v1/identity/login-by-email. Instead, the database seed at infra/postgresql/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/v0.0.0.sql:546-566 creates one user, test@featbit.com, with a password hash committed to the public repo, and the installation docs print the matching password in plain text. So WHO BECOMES THE ADMINISTRATOR: an account that exists before the first request, whose credentials are on the internet. WHEN: at the moment you apply the schema. That window is closed at DEPLOY TIME by the next quirk, not by asking the user to hurry."
  - "⛔⛔ CLOSE THAT WINDOW IN THE SAME psql RUN THAT CREATES THE SCHEMA, THEN AGAIN AFTER BOOT. Two steps, both required. STEP ONE, before the app VM ever answers: in the same session that applies the seed SQL, run UPDATE users SET email = :new_email WHERE email = 'test@featbit.com', where :new_email is an address the user gives you or an unguessable one you generate as admin-<8 lowercase alnum>@<their domain>. The published password is now useless without the address, so the instance is not claimable the second the hostname resolves. STEP TWO, as soon as the app is healthy: log in as that address with the documented default and immediately PUT /api/v1/identity/reset-password with a body of currentPassword and newPassword, then PROVE IT by logging in again with the new password and confirming the old one is refused. Do not stop at step one: an unguessable login is a delay, a rotated password is a fix."
  - "⛔ THE SCHEMA DOES NOT CREATE ITSELF, AND THIS IS THE STEP EVERY OTHER RECIPE SKIPS. FeatBit's application runs no migrations. The schema comes from ten .sql files in infra/postgresql/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/, which the stock Postgres image executes through its initdb hook, and upstream's compose bind-mounts that directory from the repository. A managed database has no initdb hook and your uploaded source has no such directory, so on redu you apply them yourself, ONCE, before the app starts: v0.0.0.sql, then v5.0.4, v5.0.5, v5.1.0, v5.2.0, v5.2.1, v5.3.0, v5.3.2, v5.4.0, v5.4.1. That is plain lexical order, which is what the Postgres image itself uses, and for these ten filenames it is also version order. If you skip this the containers still start and every request fails on a missing relation."
  - "⛔ EDIT TWO LINES OUT OF THAT SQL OR IT CANNOT WORK ON REDU, AND THE FAILURE IS THE FAMOUS ONE. v0.0.0.sql:2 is `create database featbit;` and EVERY one of the ten files begins with `\\connect featbit`. A redu managed Postgres serves exactly ONE database, because its pg_hba rules are scoped to the database it provisioned; any other database on that server is refused AT AUTHENTICATION with SQLSTATE 28000, and being a superuser does not help, because the create succeeds and the connect does not. So delete the create-database line and every connect line, and apply the remaining SQL to the database redu gave you. Then set the app's connection string to that same database. Option two, appending a pg_hba line on the database VM, works and is lost on a VM rebuild. Option three, a second managed database at GBP 0.0174/hr more, is durable and changes the quote, so it is the user's call, not yours. Option one is right here: FeatBit's tables are the only ones in that database."
  - "⛔ Jwt__Key IS THE SECRET A REDEPLOY DESTROYS, AND THE PUBLISHED PLACEHOLDER PASSES VALIDATION. The api-server validates this at startup and refuses to boot if the key equals the appsettings default or is shorter than 32 characters (modules/back-end/src/Api/Setup/JwtOptionsValidator.cs:13,42-51), which is genuinely good. The trap is that the placeholder in upstream's published compose is 39 characters and is NOT that default literal, so a stack copied verbatim starts happily with a signing key printed in a public repository, and anyone can then mint a valid session for your API. Generate your own, at least 32 alphanumeric characters, and set the identical value on every redeploy: change it and every logged-in session and every issued token stops working at once. Algorithm stays HS256; Issuer featbit and Audience featbit-api are defaults you do not need to touch."
  - "⛔ THREE BROWSER-FACING SERVICES, ONE REDU PORT. THIS IS THE SHAPE OF THE DEPLOY. Upstream expects the browser to reach the UI on 8081, the api-server on 5000 and the SDK-facing evaluation server on 5100, and to be told those absolute URLs. redu gives one proxied HTTP port on one hostname. The three route prefixes happen not to collide, which is what makes this possible: /api/v1/ belongs to the api-server (ApiControllerBase.cs:17, and upstream's own bundle nginx proxies exactly ^/api/v[\\d]/ to 5000), /api/public/ belongs to the evaluation server (PublicApiControllerBase.cs:9), /streaming is its websocket (StreamingHelper.cs:7,11), and everything else is the SPA. So add ONE nginx:1.30.4-alpine container as the front door, publish only that on port 8080, and route by those prefixes. The nginx config is in the body of this file. It was derived from those source files and has not been run by redu, so read it before you trust it."
  - "THE PUBLISHED UI IMAGE WILL NOT DO THIS FOR YOU. modules/front-end/nginx.conf.template shows the featbit-ui image is nginx serving a static SPA with no proxy_pass anywhere, and its entrypoint overwrites /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf on every start, so mounting your own config into that container is fought by the entrypoint. The separate front-door container is the clean answer, not a workaround."
  - "⛔ API_URL AND EVALUATION_URL ARE BROWSER URLS, SO GENERATE THE HOSTNAME BEFORE YOU DEPLOY. modules/front-end/docker-entrypoint.sh:30-32 runs envsubst over public/assets/env.template.js at container start and writes /assets/env.js, which the browser then reads. They must therefore be the PUBLIC https URL, never an in-compose service name and never localhost. Generate the dname yourself in full <app>-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form up front and set both API_URL and EVALUATION_URL to https://<that host>. Because everything is behind one front door they are the SAME value. DISPLAY_API_URL and DISPLAY_EVALUATION_URL are optional: sdk-endpoints.ts:17-30 falls back to the two above, and the streaming URL shown to the user is that value with http rewritten to ws, so wss://<host> is what SDKs will be told to use. envsubst substitutes every placeholder in the template, so any variable you leave unset becomes an empty string in env.js rather than a default."
  - "THE STANDALONE PROFILE NEEDS NO REDIS, NO KAFKA AND NO CLICKHOUSE, WHATEVER THE GENRE SUGGESTS. The root docker-compose.yml sets DbProvider=Postgres, MqProvider=Postgres and CacheProvider=None on both .NET services, and it starts no Redis at all; docker-compose-standard.yml is the variant that adds Redis, and the pro variant is the one with Kafka and ClickHouse. Do not provision a managed Redis or a managed ClickHouse for this recipe. If the user later outgrows Postgres as the message bus, moving to the standard profile means CacheProvider=Redis, MqProvider=Redis and Redis__ConnectionString, which is a different entry, not a tweak."
  - "DELETE THESE FROM UPSTREAM'S COMPOSE: the whole postgresql service, its named volume, and its bind mount of ./infra/postgresql/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/ (that directory is not in your upload, which is precisely why the schema step above exists); the custom featbit-network with its hardcoded [ip]/16 subnet, which has no business on a shared VM; and every host port publication except the front door's. The four application services keep talking to each other on the default compose network by service name."
  - "THE da-server IS DEPRECATED AND ITS VERSION LAGS. Upstream's own comment in docker-compose.yml calls it kept for backward compatibility and says it goes in v6.0, and it is the image with no 5.4.6 tag. It backs the analytics and insight panels and the api-server points at it with OLAP__ServiceHost=http://da-server. Keep it at 5.4.5 for a complete first deploy. Dropping it saves one container and loses the insight panels; that is a decision to put to the user, and if you drop it, drop OLAP__ServiceHost with it rather than leaving the api-server pointing at a service that is not there."
  - "DATABASE WIRING: FeatBit takes ONE connection string, not PG* variables. Both .NET services read Postgres__ConnectionString in ADO.NET form, so build it from redu's injected variables as Host=${PGHOST};Port=${PGPORT};Username=${PGUSER};Password=[REDACTED:value]};Database=${PGDATABASE} and set it on api-server AND evaluation-server. The da-server takes the same details as separate POSTGRES_HOST, POSTGRES_PORT, POSTGRES_USER, POSTGRES_PASSWORD and POSTGRES_DATABASE variables, so it needs its own mapping. deploy_compose only APPENDS the PG variables to the project .env, it never edits your compose, so the compose has to interpolate them itself. There is no SQLite fallback in this app and no bundled database once you delete the postgresql service, so a wrong connection string fails loudly rather than quietly storing data in the wrong place."
  - "PROVE THE DATABASE WIRING IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, BECAUSE A HEALTHY UI PROVES NOTHING HERE. The UI is a static SPA behind nginx and it renders perfectly with the api-server dead, so the front page is not evidence. The POSITIVE half, which also proves your command ran at all: SELECT count(*) FROM users; against the managed database must return at least 1, and SELECT email FROM users; must show the address you set, not test@featbit.com. The NEGATIVE half only means something after that: a login attempt with test@featbit.com must fail. Run them in that order."
  - "PORTS: the front-door nginx listens on 8080 and that is the ONLY port you pass to deploy_compose. Inside the compose the UI is on 80, the api-server on 5000, the evaluation server on 5100 and the da-server on 80. Do not publish those to the host. The evaluation server also exposes anonymous health/liveness and health/readiness endpoints (MiddlewaresRegister.cs:14-18) which are useful as container healthchecks and which you should NOT route through the public front door."
  - "WHAT AN ANONYMOUS REQUEST REACHES: the SPA itself, its static assets, and /assets/env.js, which by design contains your public API and evaluation URLs and nothing secret. POST /api/v1/identity/login-by-email is anonymous, as a login endpoint must be, and POST /api/v1/identity/refresh-token reads a cookie. Everything else on the api-server sits behind [Authorize] on ApiControllerBase. The SDK-facing /api/public/ routes and /streaming authenticate with per-environment SDK keys, which is the intended public surface of a feature-flag service. # Self-host FeatBit on redu

FeatBit is a feature-flag and experimentation platform: flags, targeting rules, environments, SDK
keys and an audit log, with a websocket stream that pushes flag changes to your applications in
real time. This recipe deploys the **standalone** profile, which is the Postgres-only one, on a
single VM with a managed Postgres behind it.

About GBP 0.045/hour, roughly GBP 33 a month. Inside the no-card free trial.

## What this deploys

- **nginx** as the single front door on port 8080, routing to the three services behind it.
- **featbit-ui**, the static console.
- **featbit-api-server**, the management API.
- **featbit-evaluation-server**, which your SDKs connect to, including the websocket stream.
- **featbit-data-analytics-server**, deprecated upstream but still backing the insight panels.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, holding flags, environments, users and audit logs.

No Redis, no Kafka and no ClickHouse. Those belong to FeatBit's standard and pro profiles; the
standalone one uses Postgres as its message bus and no cache at all.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy FeatBit on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The three that actually break it

**The schema does not create itself.** FeatBit's application runs no migrations. Its schema lives
in ten SQL files that the stock Postgres image executes through its initdb hook, which a managed
database does not have. The recipe applies them by hand, once, before the app starts.

**Two lines of that SQL cannot run on redu.** The first file creates a database called
`featbit` and every file then connects to it. A redu managed Postgres serves exactly one
database and refuses any other at authentication, so those lines come out and the SQL is applied
to the database redu provisioned.

**The administrator already exists, and its password is published.** The seed creates
`test@featbit.com` with a password hash committed to the repository and a plaintext password
printed in the upstream installation docs. There is no signup form to close, so the recipe renames
that account before the hostname resolves and rotates its password the moment the app is up.

## One port, three services

redu proxies a single HTTP port. FeatBit expects the browser to reach three. The prefixes do not
collide, so one nginx in front resolves it. This config is derived from the route prefixes in
upstream's source and has not been run by redu, so read it before you trust it:

```nginx
server {
  listen 8080;
  server_name _;

  # the management API
  location ~* ^/api/v[0-9]+/ {
    proxy_pass http://api-server:5000;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
  }

  # the SDK-facing API on the evaluation server
  location ^~ /api/public/ {
    proxy_pass http://evaluation-server:5100;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
  }

  # the websocket stream. Without the two upgrade headers the SDKs connect and hang.
  location ^~ /streaming {
    proxy_pass http://evaluation-server:5100;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
    proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
    proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
  }

  # everything else is the console
  location / {
    proxy_pass http://ui:80;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
  }
}
```

## Verify it after boot

The console renders whether or not the API is alive, so looking at the page proves nothing. Prove
the login instead, and prove the published credential is dead:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

HOST="${1:?usage: verify.sh <hostname.redu.cloud>}"
EMAIL="${FEATBIT_EMAIL:?export FEATBIT_EMAIL to the address you set on the seeded account}"
PASSWORD="«REDACTED:assigned:35a55f36» FEATBIT_PASSWORD to the password you rotated to}"
BASE="https://$HOST"
BODY="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$BODY"' EXIT

login() {
  # Body on stdin, never in argv: an argument is visible in ps to every user on the machine.
  printf '{"email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$1" "$2" |
    curl -sS -o "$BODY" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
      "$BASE/api/v1/identity/login-by-email"
}

# 1. Are we talking to FeatBit at all? redu's hostname answers 502 from the edge for roughly the
#    first 2.5 minutes while containers start, and an error page fails every check below for the
#    wrong reason.
code="$(curl -sS -o "$BODY" -w '%{http_code}' "$BASE/assets/env.js")"
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the edge, the stack is still starting. Re-run in a minute." >&2
  exit 75
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /assets/env.js returned $code, expected 200" >&2
  exit 75
fi
if ! grep -q 'EVALUATION_URL\|evaluationUrl' "$BODY"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: that is not FeatBit's runtime env file, so something else is answering" >&2
  exit 75
fi

# 2a. THE POSITIVE CONTROL. Without this a 401 below would mean nothing, because a broken
#     api-server refuses everyone equally.
ok="$(login "$EMAIL" "$PASSWORD")"
if [ "$ok" != "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: login with the rotated password returned $ok, expected 200" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 2b. THE NEGATIVE. The published credential must be dead, by address AND by password.
for bad_email in "test@featbit.com" "$EMAIL"; do
  bad="$(login "$bad_email" "123456")"
  if [ "$bad" = "200" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: the published default password still logs in as $bad_email." >&2
    echo "Do not leave this instance running. Rotate it now." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "OK: FeatBit is serving, your account works, and the published default is dead"
```

    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
  }

  # the websocket stream. Without the two upgrade headers the SDKs connect and hang.
  location ^~ /streaming {
    proxy_pass http://evaluation-server:5100;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
    proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
    proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
  }

  # everything else is the console
  location / {
    proxy_pass http://ui:80;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
  }
}

## Verify it after boot

The console renders whether or not the API is alive, so looking at the page proves nothing. Prove
the login instead, and prove the published credential is dead:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

HOST="${1:?usage: verify.sh <hostname.redu.cloud>}"
EMAIL="${FEATBIT_EMAIL:?export FEATBIT_EMAIL to the address you set on the seeded account}"
PASSWORD="«REDACTED:assigned:35a55f36» FEATBIT_PASSWORD to the password you rotated to}"
BASE="https://$HOST"
BODY="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$BODY"' EXIT

login() {
  # Body on stdin, never in argv: an argument is visible in ps to every user on the machine.
  printf '{"email":"%s","password":"[REDACTED:value]"}' "$1" "$2" |
    curl -sS -o "$BODY" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' --data-binary @- \
      "$BASE/api/v1/identity/login-by-email"
}

# 1. Are we talking to FeatBit at all? redu's hostname answers 502 from the edge for roughly the
#    first 2.5 minutes while containers start, and an error page fails every check below for the
#    wrong reason.
code="$(curl -sS -o "$BODY" -w '%{http_code}' "$BASE/assets/env.js")"
if [ "$code" = "502" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: 502 from the edge, the stack is still starting. Re-run in a minute." >&2
  exit 75
fi
if [ "$code" != "200" ]; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /assets/env.js returned $code, expected 200" >&2
  exit 75
fi
if ! grep -q 'EVALUATION_URL\|evaluationUrl' "$BODY"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: that is not FeatBit's runtime env file, so something else is answering" >&2
  exit 75
fi

# 2a. THE POSITIVE CONTROL. Without this a 401 below would mean nothing, because a broken
#     api-server refuses everyone equally.
ok="$(login "$EMAIL" "$PASSWORD")"
if [ "$ok" != "200" ]; then
  echo "FAIL: login with the rotated password returned $ok, expected 200" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# 2b. THE NEGATIVE. The published credential must be dead, by address AND by password.
for bad_email in "test@featbit.com" "$EMAIL"; do
  bad="$(login "$bad_email" "123456")"
  if [ "$bad" = "200" ]; then
    echo "FAIL: the published default password still logs in as $bad_email." >&2
    echo "Do not leave this instance running. Rotate it now." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "OK: FeatBit is serving, your account works, and the published default is dead"
```

BEFORE plan_deploy, cat these three files from the repo root if they exist and pass them to plan_deploy VERBATIM: redu.md (as redu_md), the compose file (as compose_yaml), and the Dockerfile (as dockerfile). Do NOT read or summarise them - redu parses them SERVER-SIDE and returns a short digest, a pin_dname that keeps a redeploy on the SAME public URL, and preflight fixes for known failure patterns in YOUR repo. Highest-value step in the flow; it costs one cat each. KEEP the redu.md bytes: pass them to get_deployment as redu_md at the end too, so redu merges the old file with the new deploy instead of you overwriting what previous deploys learned.
platform_facts: THE deploy VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN. The compose project is named app-src, so containers are app-src-<service>-1 and volumes are app-src_<name>. Use `sudo docker ...` on the VM; podman is not installed. Several deploys rediscovered this independently.

SOURCE IS EITHER GIT OR UPLOAD, NEVER BOTH. For code that is not pushed, or is private, or needs fixing first: write the files locally, call prepare_upload, run the tar+curl block it returns, then pass the source_token and NO repo. ⚠️ prepare_upload EXCLUDES .env from the tarball by design, so secrets have to reach the VM another way (pass them to the deploy call, not in the tree).

A MANAGED DATABASE IS A SECOND VM WITH ITS OWN HOURLY RATE, and delete_deployment deliberately LEAVES IT BEHIND so your data survives the app. That means a teardown that stops at delete_deployment keeps billing a database nobody can reach. Call delete_database too, and say so to the user before either.

A MANAGED POSTGRES SERVES EXACTLY ONE DATABASE. pg_hba is evaluated before role privileges, so being superuser does not help. An app that wants a second database needs a second managed server. This has broken deploys that otherwise looked healthy.

get_deployment RETURNS THE MERGED redu.md ONLY WHEN IT FITS ITS RESPONSE BUDGET. Over budget - which is normal for a mature recipe or any large app - it withholds redu_md_markdown and returns redu_md_last_deploy_block plus redu_md_deploy_log_line instead. That is NOT an error and must not be retried: apply those two edits to the file on disk and change nothing else.

⛔ THE MERGE NEVER WRITES A NEW QUIRK. Whatever redu returns, it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line and nothing else. Every gotcha YOUR run discovered has to be typed into the quirks list by hand before you commit, or it is lost - and that list is the only part of the file that makes the next deploy cheaper.
⛔ NEVER WRITE A CREDENTIAL INTO redu.md. It is committed and read by the next person and the next agent. Names of variables, yes; their values, never. Hand secrets to the user in the session instead.

plan_deploy OVER-SIZES A PULLED COMPOSE STACK. Measured 8 times out of 8: declaring needs_compose makes it quote m1.large, roughly double the real requirement, because it cannot see that the images are pulled rather than built. Show the user the plan, but size from the app's real memory figure when you have one.

THE MANAGED DATABASE PASSWORD IS ON THE VM, NOT IN THE API. list_databases returns private_ip, port, db_name and db_user and DELIBERATELY NOT the password, so an agent that looks for it there finds nothing and starts guessing. The deploy writes the whole connection set into the compose project's .env on the app VM. Call get_env_keys for the NAMES first (no SSH, values never leave the VM); only if you need an actual VALUE, SSH in (get_ssh_command) and read that one key, `sudo grep '^PGPASSWORD=' /opt/app-src/.env`. ⚠️ That file is chmod 600 root:root so it needs sudo, and the database is on the PRIVATE network - reachable from the app VM, never from a laptop.

YOU CAN READ A DEPLOY VM WITHOUT SSHING INTO IT, and four tools do it: get_containers (what is running, health, restarts, crashed ones included), get_container_logs (what the app actually printed - the tool for 'deployed fine but does not work'), get_resource_usage (memory, disk, load, OOM kills) and get_env_keys (which variables got wired, by name). ⛔ get_instance_logs is the SERIAL CONSOLE and is not your app's logs; build_log stops when the build does. SSH is still yours for everything else - a shell on a real machine is the point, not a fallback. ⭐ MEASURED over 38 deploys: of 241 ssh escapes, 146 (61%) were exactly these four things, and the four tools were called 11 times. They are faster than a login, they cost the VM nothing extra (the reading is already cached), and reaching for ssh to run `docker ps` is the single most common wasted minute in a deploy.

⛔ THE PRIMARY SURFACE'S HOSTNAME COMES FROM THE TOP-LEVEL dname, NOT FROM expose[0].dname, WHICH IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. Extra expose entries DO keep the dname you give them, so the two behave differently and nothing tells you. If an app bakes its own public URL into config at boot (CPAD_MAIN_DOMAIN, allowed_origins, SITE_URL), generate the full `<label>-<8 lowercase letters/digits>.redu.cloud` form yourself and pass it as the TOP-LEVEL dname, which is used verbatim. Passing it on expose[0] instead gets you an app configured for a hostname redu never created, answering 200 on a name it does not believe is its own.

WEBSOCKETS WORK THROUGH THE PROXY WITH NO CONFIGURATION: every proxy host redu creates has upgrade enabled. Measured at the protocol level, HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols with the subprotocol echoed back. ⚠️ TEST IT WITH `curl --http1.1`: plain curl negotiates HTTP/2, which has no Upgrade mechanism at all, so the app answers as an ordinary GET and the failure looks exactly like a proxy refusing to upgrade. Browsers use HTTP/1.1 for websockets regardless. Do not disable an app's realtime features on the strength of an HTTP/2 curl.

# FeatBit standalone profile for redu.cloud.

#
# Removed from upstream's compose, deliberately:

      - EVALUATION_URL=${PUBLIC_URL}

input.redu_md:
---
redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/featbit/featbit
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: featbit/featbit-ui:5.4.5 + featbit-api-server:5.4.5 + featbit-evaluation-server:5.4.5 + featbit-data-analytics-server:5.4.5 + nginx:1.30.4-alpine
  port: 8080
  vm: m1.medium
  flavor_id: "3"
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.0452
bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: featbit
quirks:
  - "PIN THE WHOLE STACK AT 5.4.5. featbit-ui, api-server and evaluation-server publish 5.4.6; data-analytics-server stops at 5.4.5. 5.4.5 is the newest tag that exists for all four. Never :latest."
  - "NOBODY SIGNS UP, AND THE ADMINISTRATOR ALREADY EXISTS WITH A PUBLISHED PASSWORD. The seed creates test@featbit.com with a hash committed to the public repo. Rename it in the same psql run that applies the schema, then rotate the password after boot."
  - "THE SCHEMA DOES NOT CREATE ITSELF. Ten .sql files in infra/postgresql/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/ applied by hand, once, in lexical order, before the app starts."
  - "EDIT TWO LINES OUT OF THAT SQL: v0.0.0.sql:2 create database featbit; and every \\connect featbit line. A redu managed Postgres serves exactly ONE database."
  - "Jwt__Key IS THE SECRET A REDEPLOY DESTROYS. Generate 32+ alphanumeric chars and set the identical value on every redeploy."
  - "THREE BROWSER-FACING SERVICES, ONE REDU PORT. One nginx:1.30.4-alpine front door on 8080 routes /api/v[0-9]+/ to api-server:5000, /api/public/ and /streaming to evaluation-server:5100, everything else to ui:80."
  - "API_URL AND EVALUATION_URL ARE BROWSER URLS. Generate the dname up front in full <app>-<8 lowercase alnum>.redu.cloud form and set both to https://<that host>."

content.text:
I've written the plan to `redu-deploy-plan.md`. Here it is:

**FeatBit 5.4.5, standalone profile — 2 VMs**

| Resource | Rate | Monthly (730h) |
|---|---|---|
| App VM — m1.medium (2 vCPU / 4 GB) | £0.0278/hr | £20.29 |
| Managed Postgres 16 — m1.small (1 vCPU / 2 GB) | £0.0174/hr | £12.70 |
| **Total** | **£0.0452/hr** | **£33.00** |

Five containers on one VM: `nginx` front door on 8080 → `featbit-ui`, `api-server` (`/api/v[0-9]+/`), `evaluation-server` (`/api/public/` + `/streaming` websocket), plus the `da-server` behind the API. Postgres is on its own private VM, unreachable from the internet.

Two things worth flagging before you say go:

**I'm overriding `plan_deploy`'s sizing.** It quoted m1.large at £48.18/mo. It up-sizes every compose stack because it can't tell that all five images are *pulled* rather than built — nothing here compiles. redu.md records m1.medium as what actually ran, so I'm passing `flavor_id: "3"` explicitly, which is the £33/mo figure above. If it turns out tight, the upgrade is m1.mem16, not m1.large.

**FeatBit has no signup form, and its administrator already exists with a published password.** The database seed creates `test@featbit.com` with a hash committed to the public repo and the plaintext printed in upstream's docs. So I close that window in two steps: rename the account in the same psql run that creates the schema (before the hostname ever resolves), then rotate the password once the app is up and prove the old one is refused. That's why I need an address from you.

Public URL will be `https://featbit-2kjxmfvq.redu.cloud` — generated up front because the browser bundle bakes it in at container start.

content.text:
The monitor is armed and will notify me the moment Postgres accepts connections. Current state of the deploy:

**Done**
- Managed Postgres 16 created (`featbit-db`, id 153, m1.small) — VM ACTIVE at private `[ip]`, cloud-init still installing Postgres
- Source packaged and uploaded (compose + nginx front-door config, 1582 bytes, size confirmed against the server's echo)
- Ten schema files fetched at tag 5.4.5; `create database featbit;` and all ten `\connect featbit` lines stripped; verified no psql meta-commands or transaction-hostile statements survive
- Admin rename folded into the *same* file as the schema, wrapped with a fail-closed assertion that aborts the transaction if `test@featbit.com` still exists or the rename doesn't land exactly once — so there is no committed state in which the published credential works
- Seed file staged on the DB VM, SHA-256 verified end to end

**Next, once Postgres answers:** apply the seed in one `--single-transaction` psql run → `deploy_compose` (flavor_id 3, port 8080, pinned dname, PG*/JWT_KEY/PUBLIC_URL passed as env) → rotate the admin password → run the two-directional verification.

Two notes on choices I made that differ from redu.md's literal text, both of which I'll write back into the file:

**I'm passing `database:'compose'`, not `database:'managed'`, to `deploy_compose`.** The recipe says to create the managed database first *and* to pass `database:'managed'`. Those two instructions conflict — `database:'managed'` provisions a *second* Postgres VM and wires the app to that empty one, which would both double the database bill and point FeatBit at a schema-less database. Since I created and seeded the database myself, I'll pass the connection details explicitly via `env` instead. One database, and it's the seeded one.

**The 5.4.5 pin's stated reason is now stale** — `featbit-data-analytics-server:5.4.6` was published today at 02:07 UTC. I'm still deploying 5.4.5 as approved and verified; 5.4.6 ships the same ten schema files if you want the bump later.

First, FeatBit's login endpoint returns HTTP 200 for a FAILED login, with a body of success:false and errors:[EmailPasswordMismatch]. The old script compared HTTP STATUS CODES, so its negative check fired on every single run and announced that the published default still logs in when it does not - a security check that cried wolf unconditionally. Parse the JSON success field, never the status code. Second, /assets/env.js does not exist, so the old first check 404'd forever and every run exited INCONCLUSIVE before reaching a single login. Both halves of that script were therefore inert. If you change it again, run it once against a KNOWN-BAD password and confirm it actually fails.",
 "THE CONSOLE IS LOCALIZED AND / IS A REDIRECT, WHICH MOVES env.js. The featbit-ui image serves from /usr/share/nginx/featbit and its bundled config rewrites ^/$ to the Accept-Language match, so / returns 301 to /en (or /zh). The runtime config the browser actually reads is at /en/assets/env.js and /zh/assets/env.js, NEVER /assets/env.js. Route / to the ui as normal, the redirect is served to the browser and works fine, but point health checks and any env.js assertion at /en/assets/env.js.",

BODY="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$BODY"' EXIT

login() {

    | curl -sS -o "$BODY" -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' \\
        --data-binary @- "$BASE/api/v1/identity/login-by-email" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo error; return; }

  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: /en/assets/env.js returned $code, expected 200" >&2
  exit 75
fi
if ! grep -q 'evaluationUrl' "$BODY"; then
  echo "INCONCLUSIVE: that is not FeatBit's runtime env file, so something else is answering" >&2

FeatBit is deployed and verified.

**https://featbit-2kjxmfvq.redu.cloud**

| | |
|---|---|
| Admin | `«REDACTED:env:013044ef»` |
| Password | `«REDACTED:entropy:5e48bc3b»` |
| `Jwt__Key` | `«REDACTED:entropy:f591d1df»` |
| DB password | `«REDACTED:entropy:77d64fc5»` (user/db `featbit`, `[ip]:5432`) |
| Cost | £0.0452/hr — **£33/mo**, as planned |

Secrets are in `.secrets/values.env` (mode 600), and I confirmed by grep that none of them appear in `redu.md`, `redu-deploy-plan.md`, or the uploaded stack. Reuse that `Jwt__Key` verbatim on any redeploy — changing it invalidates every session and token at once.

**Verified, not assumed:** 32 tables in the managed Postgres, one user, zero rows for `test@featbit.com`. Login with the new password succeeds; the published default fails both against the renamed address and against `test@featbit.com`. The websocket returns `101 Switching Protocols` with the app answering behind it, and the evaluation server's `/health/readiness` returns 200, which is independent proof of its own database wiring. All five containers healthy.

**Four things I had to correct in redu.md, all now written back as quirks:**

**The verify script in the recipe could never have passed.** Two independent bugs. It polls `/assets/env.js`, but the console is localized — `/` 301s to `/en` and the file lives at `/en/assets/env.js`, so every run exited INCONCLUSIVE before reaching a single login. And more seriously, it compares HTTP status codes, but FeatBit returns **200 for a failed login** with `success:false` in the body. Had the first check passed, the security assertion would have reported "the published default password still logs in" on every run forever. I rewrote it to parse the JSON `success` field, ran it (passes), then ran it with a deliberately wrong password to confirm it actually fails. It does.

**The recipe's deploy step contradicted itself.** It says to create and seed the database first, then to call `deploy_compose` with `database:'managed'` — which provisions a *second* Postgres and wires the app to the empty one. That would have doubled the database bill and pointed FeatBit at a schema-less database, the exact failure the file exists to prevent. I used `database:'compose'` and passed the connection details through `env`.

**The 5.4.5 pin's stated reason expired six days after it was written** — `featbit-data-analytics-server:5.4.6` was pushed today at 02:07 UTC. All four images now publish 5.4.6, and its git tree ships the same ten schema files, so a bump needs no migration. I stayed on 5.4.5 as approved.

**Sizing:** `plan_deploy` quoted m1.large at £48.18/mo; I measured actual idle use at **1078 MB of 3915** (~480 MB of containers, da-server the largest at 311 MB). m1.medium is comfortable, and that number is now in the file so the next run doesn't have to re-derive it.

One thing I did *not* change, per the recipe's advice: the evaluation server ships `Cors.AllowedOrigins: "*"` and `RateLimiting.Enabled: false`. The wildcard CORS is correct for a service browser SDKs call from your own domains — narrowing it breaks them. But rate limiting being off means an unauthenticated flood of connection attempts isn't throttled at the app layer. Worth turning on (`RateLimiting.Enabled`, `PermitLimit`, `WindowSeconds`) before you point real traffic at it.

Note for teardown: `delete_deployment` deliberately leaves the database running at £0.0174/hr. It holds every flag, environment and SDK key, and recreating it means applying those ten SQL files again — so call `delete_database` explicitly when you actually want it gone.
